Foreign Currency

Define foreign currencies for multi-currency transactions.

Set currency code, symbol, and decimal places for accurate display.

Code

Enter the three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, such as 'USD' for US Dollar, 'EUR' for Euro, 'GBP' for British Pound, or 'JPY' for Japanese Yen.

Using standard currency codes ensures consistency and helps with exchange rate lookups and international transactions.

The code appears throughout the system to identify this currency and is used when importing exchange rates.

Name

Enter the full name of the currency, such as 'US Dollar', 'Euro', 'British Pound', or 'Japanese Yen'.

The name helps users identify the currency in dropdown menus and reports, especially when multiple currencies are in use.

Use the official currency name for clarity and professional appearance on documents.

Prefix

Enter the currency symbol that will appear with amounts as prefix, such as '$' for dollars, '€' for euros, '£' for pounds, or '¥' for yen.

The symbol is displayed before or after amounts depending on your locale settings and makes financial data easier to read at a glance.

Suffix

Enter the currency symbol that will appear with amounts as suffix, such as '$' for dollars, '€' for euros, '£' for pounds, or '¥' for yen.

The symbol is displayed before or after amounts depending on your locale settings and makes financial data easier to read at a glance.

Decimal places

Specify the number of decimal places for this currency. Most currencies use 2 decimal places (e.g., $1.50), but some use different amounts.

For example, Japanese Yen typically uses 0 decimal places (¥1,000), while some Middle Eastern currencies use 3 decimal places.

This setting ensures amounts are displayed and rounded correctly throughout the system.

Inactive

Mark this foreign currency as inactive to hide it from dropdown lists while preserving all historical transactions.

Use this when you no longer transact in this currency but need to keep records of past transactions for reporting purposes.

Inactive currencies can be reactivated at any time if you resume trading in that currency.
